chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Bashir from Ibn Abi Ya'fur said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from our companions entered upon him and said to him, 'May Allah rectify you. Indeed, sometimes hardship or distress befalls one of us, so he is called upon to build a structure (he builds it), or to rent out a canal (he rents it), or to repair a mill (he repairs it). What do you say regarding that?'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'I would not like that a knot or a tying be tied for them, and that there be for me what is between their two ends, neither for a specific period nor for a duration, written with a pen. Indeed, the assistants of the oppressors on the Day of Resurrection are in a tent of fire until Allah judges between the servants.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on building or renting property when called upon during hardship, according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on *khiraj* (rental income) from public utilities like canals and mills, expressing a preference against binding contracts that fix duration or share via written deed, likely to avoid the uncertainty (*gharar*) or exploitation associated with state-imposed levies. He characterizes those who facilitate these revenues as 'assistants of the oppressors' (*aw'an al-zalima*), linking their financial role to spiritual accountability in the Hereafter. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between legitimate private rental and revenue streams tied to governance or taxation.
